children: Jaguar Health, Inc.
) shares are trending on Tuesday night.

Shares of the San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company jumped 5.19% to $36.25 in after-hours trading, following the Food and Drug Administration’s decision to waive key prescription drug fees for two of its therapies.
FDA Waives Fees On HIV/AIDS Drug
Napo Pharmaceuticals

, Jaguar Health’s family company, said the FDA granted a waiver of the Prescription Drug User Fee Act fee for Mytesi crofelemer delayed-release tablets for fiscal year 2027, the company announced Tuesday. Mytesi is approved for symptomatic relief of noninfectious diarrhea in adult HIV/AIDS patients on antiretroviral therapy and is commercialized in the U.S. by Michigan-based pharmaceutical and nutraceutical packager and manufacturer
Future Pak, LLC
Separately, the FDA’s Center for Veterinary Medicine waived fees for Canalevia-CA1, Jaguar’s conditionally approved drug treating chemotherapy-induced diarrhea in dogs, also marketed by Future Pak.
Trading Metrics, Technical Analysis
Jaguar Health has a market capitalization of $13.73 million, a 52-week high of $1,280.95 and a 52-week low of $2.37. The company has approximately 345,000 shares outstanding.
The Relative Strength Index (RSI) of JAGX stands at 81.09.
The small-cap stock has fallen 96.77% over the past 12 months.
JAGX is currently trading very close to its annual low.
